issues.legal_issue: An arbitral valuation based on relevant material and supported by reasons is not open to reappraisal as a factual determination merely because a party disputes the chosen valuation.
material_facts: The dissolution agreement contemplated valuation by a government-approved valuer.
The valuer’s report was admitted as an exhibit with both parties’ consent and without reservation.
The arbitrator considered the report, competing expert evidence and other valuation material, and gave reasons for the values selected.
issues.conclusion: The valuation findings were upheld because the arbitrator relied on proper material and gave sufficient reasons, and the court would not re-examine the factual merits of the valuation.
issues.legal_principle: A court reviewing an arbitral award does not delve into the details of factual valuation or decide whether particular items or evidence should have been accepted where the arbitrator has considered the material and given reasons. The report did not require formal proof because it was admitted by consent without reservation. The judgment cited no earlier case as the basis for this conclusion.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenged: A party challenged a factual valuation made in an arbitral award.
predicates.valuation_based_on_relevant_material: The arbitrator considered relevant valuation material, including evidence bearing on the competing valuations.
predicates.arbitrator_gave_reasons: The arbitrator explained the basis for selecting the valuation.

issues.definition: When a challenged arbitral valuation rests on relevant material and reasons, the valuation finding is upheld rather than reappraised as a factual matter.

issues.legal_issue: Admitting an expert valuation report by consent without reservation dispenses with formal proof of the report, and declining a late request for an adjournment to present further evidence does not necessarily amount to misconduct.
material_facts: The parties consented to the government-approved valuer’s report being made an exhibit without reservation.
The request to summon that valuer for cross-examination had been made by the applicants, while the objectors did not request it at that stage and examined their own expert.

The objectors sought an adjournment late in the proceedings for a party to give evidence, after agreeing to day-to-day proceedings; their expert had already testified and the valuer’s report was on record.
The venue change was acquiesced in by both sides.
issues.conclusion: The report did not require formal proof, and neither the venue change nor the refusal of the late adjournment request constituted misconduct on these facts.
issues.legal_principle: An expert report admitted by consent without reservation need not be formally proved by calling its author. The judgment considered the timing and circumstances of the adjournment request and the parties’ acquiescence in the venue change in deciding whether the arbitrator had misconducted the proceedings. Although counsel cited U.P. Hotels v. U.P. State Electricity Board, Ahmedabad Municipality v. Shantilal, Payyavula Vengamma v. Payyavula Kesanna, and Perumal Mudaliar v. S.I. Railway Co., the court resolved the issue on the particular circumstances and did not apply those cases as the basis for its ruling.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenged: A party alleged that the arbitrator’s procedure invalidated the award.
predicates.report_admitted_by_consent_without_reser: The parties accepted an expert report into the arbitration record without reserving an objection to its admission.
predicates.late_evidence_request: A party sought an adjournment to present further evidence only at a late stage of the arbitration.
predicates.venue_change_acquiesced_in: Both sides accepted the change in the place where the arbitration proceedings were held.

issues.definition: In a challenge to an arbitral award, consent to admission of a report and acquiescence in a venue change, together with a late request for further evidence, do not by themselves establish procedural misconduct.

issues.legal_issue: A party’s use of an inventory valuation to support interim relief does not by itself admit that the inventory states the goods’ correct value.
material_facts: A party relied on an inventory’s approximate valuation in a proceeding seeking to prevent the other group from alienating goods.
That party maintained that the inventory had been received subject to checking and had not accepted its figures as correct.
The arbitrator considered the valuation independently.
issues.conclusion: The use of the inventory in support of interim relief was not an admission of the goods’ value, and the arbitrator was entitled to determine that value independently.
issues.legal_principle: A valuation used to support an interim request to preserve property does not, without more, amount to an admission that the valuation is correct. The arbitrator may determine the valuation independently. The judgment relied on no earlier case for this conclusion.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenged: A party challenged a valuation finding in an arbitral award.
predicates.inventory_used_to_preserve_property: A party relied on an inventory valuation to seek an order preventing property from being alienated.
predicates.inventory_not_accepted_as_correct: The party had not accepted the inventory’s stated figures as the correct valuation.

issues.definition: Using an inventory valuation to preserve property, without accepting it as correct, does not make that valuation an admission in the arbitration.

issues.legal_issue: Specific contractual allocations of bank liabilities govern over a general provision for sharing debts and expenses.
material_facts: The dissolution agreement separately assigned responsibility for each of two banks’ accounts and liabilities to different partner groups.
A general clause provided for equal sharing of debts, credits and expenses.
The group assigned responsibility for one bank sought contribution because that bank’s liabilities exceeded the liabilities assigned to the other group.
issues.conclusion: Each group remained responsible for the liabilities assigned to it, and the general sharing clause did not require contribution for the excess of one bank’s liabilities.
issues.legal_principle: The agreement’s specific provisions allocating bank accounts and their associated responsibilities govern over a general or residuary provision for sharing debts and expenses. The court relied on the terms of the dissolution agreement and no earlier case.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenged: A party challenged an arbitrator’s interpretation of contractual allocations.
predicates.agreement_specifically_allocates_bank_li: The agreement assigns responsibility for identified bank accounts or liabilities to particular groups.
predicates.agreement_has_general_debt_sharing_claus: The agreement also contains a general provision for sharing debts or expenses.

issues.definition: Where an agreement both specifically allocates bank liabilities and generally shares debts, the specific allocation controls.

issues.legal_issue: A specific agreement assigning responsibility for employees of separate business units governs employee payments other than those expressly agreed to be shared.
material_facts: The agreement assigned each group responsibility for employees at the factory allocated to that group.
It expressly provided that gratuity for workers of both factories would be shared equally.
The arbitrator treated other employee payments, including bonus, medical expenses and leave encashment, as the responsibility of the group assigned the relevant factory.
issues.conclusion: The specific employee-liability provision governed, so payments other than gratuity were not shared under the general debt-sharing clause.
issues.legal_principle: A specific contractual provision governing a category of liability to employees controls over a general clause concerning debts and expenses; an express exception for one payment does not extend to other payments. The court relied on the agreement’s terms and no earlier case.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenged: A party challenged an arbitrator’s interpretation of employee-related liabilities.
predicates.agreement_assigns_unit_employee_responsi: The agreement assigns responsibility for employees of separate business units to the groups taking over those units.
predicates.agreement_expressly_shares_only_a_specif: The agreement expressly makes one category of employee payment a shared liability while not extending that treatment to other categories.

issues.definition: If a contract assigns unit-related employee responsibility and expressly shares only a specified employee payment, the other employee payments remain with the group assigned that unit.

issues.legal_issue: A deposit pledged with a bank as part of the dealings allocated to one group belongs to that group when the agreement assigns that group the bank dealings and related liabilities.
material_facts: A fixed deposit with a bank had been pledged to secure an advance connected with a contract undertaken by one group.
The agreement assigned that group responsibility for the dealings with that bank and for the related bank liabilities.
The agreement expressly treated a mortgaged factory block as a divisible factory asset but did not provide comparable treatment for the fixed deposit.
issues.conclusion: The fixed deposit was the exclusive property of the group responsible for the bank dealings and was not divisible between the groups.
issues.legal_principle: Where a contract allocates the entirety of dealings with a bank and its liabilities to one group, a deposit pledged as security in those dealings is treated as part of those dealings and allocated to that group, absent a contrary contractual provision. The court relied on the agreement’s interpretation and no earlier case.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenged: A party challenged an arbitrator’s allocation of a business asset.
predicates.agreement_assigns_bank_dealings_to_one_g: The agreement assigns responsibility for all dealings with a particular bank to one group.
predicates.deposit_pledged_in_those_dealings: A deposit was pledged with that bank as security in dealings allocated to that group.

issues.definition: A deposit pledged in bank dealings assigned to one group is allocated to that group rather than divided when the agreement provides no contrary treatment.

issues.legal_issue: A general division of business assets is not displaced by a group’s sole responsibility for a contract when the evidence does not establish that the assets were acquired for that contract.
material_facts: One group had taken over a contract and accepted responsibility for its performance and for repaying an advance connected with it.
The objectors argued that machinery and materials associated with the contract should therefore be assigned to that group alone.
There was no record or evidence establishing that the relevant raw material or stock had been purchased out of the contract advance.
The agreement provided for the valuation and division of raw materials and goods at the business units.
issues.conclusion: The arbitrator’s division of the raw materials and goods was upheld because there was no evidence connecting them to the advance or establishing that they were contract-specific assets.
issues.legal_principle: A party asserting that assets are excluded from a general contractual division must establish the factual connection supporting that exclusion; the agreement’s general asset-division provisions remain applicable where that connection is not proved. The court relied on the agreement and the absence of evidence, without citing an earlier case.

rule.if: arbitration_award_challenged and agreement_divides_business_stock and contract_liability_assigned_to_one_group and no_evidence_links_stock_to_contract_advance

predicates.arbitration_award_challenged: A party challenged an arbitrator’s division of business assets.
predicates.agreement_divides_business_stock: The agreement provides for valuation and division of business stock or goods.
predicates.contract_liability_assigned_to_one_group: One group accepted responsibility for performing a business contract and repaying its associated advance.
predicates.no_evidence_links_stock_to_contract_adva: The record does not establish that the stock was acquired with the contract advance or otherwise belonged exclusively to the contract.

issues.definition: When a contract liability is assigned to one group but the evidence does not link business stock to the contract advance, the agreed general division of stock remains effective.

issues.legal_issue: An objection about the burden of proving accounting entries does not justify interference with an arbitral finding after the arbitrator has examined the accounts and the available material in detail.
material_facts: A party argued that the other group, which maintained the accounts, had to prove the truth of their entries.
The arbitrator examined the accounts, considered the individual items and addressed the objections in detail before reaching findings.
issues.conclusion: The court declined to interfere because the arbitrator had considered the full material and the alleged inaccuracies presented questions of fact.
issues.legal_principle: The burden-of-proof objection does not warrant intervention where the arbitrator has examined the relevant material and reached findings on it; disputes about the correctness of entries are factual. The judgment relied on no earlier case for this conclusion.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenged: A party challenged an arbitrator’s findings about accounts.
predicates.arbitrator_examined_accounts_and_objecti: The arbitrator considered the accounts, relevant entries and the parties’ objections before making findings.

issues.definition: When an arbitrator has examined the accounts and objections in detail, the court does not reopen the resulting factual findings merely because a party disputes the burden of proving entries.

issues.legal_issue: An arithmetical error in an arbitral award that is established and accepted by the parties may be corrected.
material_facts: The objectors identified arithmetical errors in the interim award.
The applicants conceded that the claimed errors were correct and agreed that the award could be rectified.
issues.conclusion: The award was directed to be rectified to correct the conceded arithmetical errors.
issues.legal_principle: The court corrected the identified arithmetical errors where their correctness was conceded. The judgment relied on no cited provision or earlier case for this direction.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenged: A party sought correction of an arbitral award.
predicates.arithmetic_error_identified: A party identified a computational error in the award.
predicates.other_party_concedes_error: The opposing party accepted that the identified computational error was correct.

issues.definition: An identified computational error in an award is corrected when the opposing party concedes it.

issues.legal_issue: An arbitrator deciding disputes referred from a pending suit has the court’s power to award interest within the referred dispute, including pendente lite interest where the agreement does not prohibit it and interest is within the claim referred.
material_facts: The disputes pending in civil suits, together with disputes under the dissolution agreement, were referred to arbitration.
The agreement contemplated payment of interest and did not prohibit an award of interest.
The claim and reference were broad enough to include interest.
issues.conclusion: The arbitrator could award pendente lite interest, but the award was modified so that interest would run only after a reasonable period for valuation and assessment under the agreement.
issues.legal_principle: A Constitution Bench in Secretary, Irrigation Department v. G.C. Roy, [1992] 1 SCC 508, held that an arbitrator may award pendente lite interest where the agreement does not prohibit it and the interest dispute is referred, subject to the arbitrator’s discretion. Section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure informs the power to award interest. Where disputes pending in a suit are referred, the arbitrator has the powers the court would have in deciding those issues. The agreement’s interest provision and valuation process controlled the appropriate commencement of interest here.

rule.if: pending_suit_referred_to_arbitration and interest_claim_within_reference and agreement_does_not_prohibit_interest and agreement_sets_interest_trigger

predicates.pending_suit_referred_to_arbitration: A dispute already pending for adjudication in a suit was referred to arbitration.
predicates.interest_claim_within_reference: The claim for interest was included in the dispute referred to the arbitrator.
predicates.agreement_does_not_prohibit_interest: The parties’ agreement does not prohibit the award of interest.
predicates.agreement_sets_interest_trigger: The agreement specifies an event or process that governs when interest becomes payable.

issues.definition: When a pending suit is referred to arbitration, an included interest claim is not barred if the agreement permits interest, but the award must respect the agreement’s interest trigger.

issues.legal_issue: The power to award pendente lite interest does not establish a general power to award pre-reference interest, which is governed by substantive law.
material_facts: The reference arose before the Interest Act, 1978 came into force.
The arbitrator awarded interest for a period before the reference as well as for the period during the reference.
The agreement contemplated interest from the valuation of assets, while the valuation process required a reasonable time.
issues.conclusion: The pre-reference award was not justified on the facts; interest was allowed only after a reasonable period for valuation and assessment, and not from the date of dissolution.
issues.legal_principle: Secretary, Irrigation Department v. G.C. Roy, [1992] 1 SCC 508, concerned pendente lite interest and did not overrule Executive Engineer, Irrigation, Galimala v. Abaaduta Jena, [1988] 1 SCR 253, as to pre-reference interest. Interest for the period before reference is a matter of substantive law, unlike pendente lite interest. Seth Thawardas Pherumal v. Union of India, [1955] 2 SCR 48, remained relevant to the limits on pre-reference interest. The contractual interest provision and the need to allow a reasonable time for valuation also informed the modification.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenged: A party challenged an arbitral award of interest.
predicates.interest_claim_covers_pre_reference_peri: The interest awarded includes time before the dispute was referred to arbitration.
predicates.reference_precedes_applicable_interest_l: The arbitration reference occurred before the relevant interest legislation applied.
predicates.agreement_ties_interest_to_valuation: The agreement makes interest payable by reference to valuation or assessment of the assets.

issues.definition: Where a challenged award includes pre-reference interest and the agreement ties interest to valuation, pre-reference interest is not awarded without a substantive legal basis.

issues.legal_issue: Title deeds held by a bank after its secured dues have been cleared may be delivered to a representative agreed upon by all concerned parties when the bank has no other claim to them.
material_facts: The parties represented before the court agreed that the title deeds could be returned to one person on behalf of the estate and all concerned family members.
The court directed return only if the bank’s dues had been cleared and it had no other claim on the deeds.
The recipient was to hold the deeds on behalf of the estate, not in an individual capacity.
issues.conclusion: The bank was directed to return the deeds to the agreed representative on the stated conditions, who would hold them for the estate.
issues.legal_principle: Once secured dues are cleared and the bank has no other claim to title deeds, it has no basis to retain them; where all concerned parties agree on a representative, delivery may be made to that person in a representative capacity. The judgment relied on no cited provision or earlier case.

rule.if: bank_holds_title_deeds_as_security and secured_dues_cleared and no_other_bank_claim and parties_agree_on_representative

predicates.bank_holds_title_deeds_as_security: A bank retains title deeds that were deposited as security for a debt or advance.
predicates.secured_dues_cleared: The debt secured by the title deeds has been fully paid.
predicates.no_other_bank_claim: The bank has no other claim relating to the title deeds.
predicates.parties_agree_on_representative: All concerned parties agree that a specified person may receive the deeds on their behalf.

issues.definition: When secured dues are cleared, the bank has no remaining claim and the parties agree on a representative, the deeds are returned to that representative.
